eval.title: Hershey Stock Analysis NYSE: HSY

call.headline_quote: so not a relative buy it is not an absolute buy for just a 3% dividend

base_metric.name: fcf_per_share
base_metric.quote: we can do EV valuation based on Fast numbers

scenarios.name: worst
scenarios.quote: the margin of safety buy would be let's say at 50% down because somebody would then buy the brands for 1.5 billion in cash flows that's 77.7% yield

what_is_priced_in.quote: the market liked it was willing to pay 40 times earnings a year ago but that doesn't tell me much

reasons.claim: A 5x spike in cocoa prices could halve Hershey's net profits if it persists, which is why the stock has fallen.
reasons.quote: so they could lose half of their net profits if the current situation persists for longer and that is why the stock is down

reasons.claim: Even after the drop the stock still trades at a P/E of 25 for flat earnings, which is not cheap.
reasons.quote: even now with the stock being down significantly the p ratio is still 25

data_check.gap_note: he says 25, as-of 20.5662 (FY2023); annual vs TTM or a different definition

reasons.claim: Management says it is committed to pricing through cocoa inflation but this is easy to claim and depends on customers and competitors accepting it.
reasons.quote: we are committed to pricing to cover inflation okay you are committed but if the customer doesn't like it or you can't or other competitors don't do it so it's just easy to say

reasons.claim: Hershey pays a growing dividend and does buybacks, but the current 3% yield is not compelling enough on its own.
reasons.quote: repurchasing about 300 million but not that significant 900 million of dividends for a 3e% dividend yield

data_check.gap_note: he says 300, as-of -2.64913e+08 (FY2023); annual vs TTM or a different definition

reasons.claim: Cocoa is a cyclical input and historically these price spikes eventually retreat, but the timing is unknowable, so the market is pricing in continued uncertainty.
reasons.quote: if the speculators keep cornering the market it will stay there for longer

external_facts_used: Bank of America analyst question in the earnings conference call about cocoa price durability
management (Michelle) comment that they've seen similar cost cycles before
historical cocoa price spike in the 1970s

critic.notes: ok — he rejects relative and absolute buy, sees margin-of-safety only ~50% lower, 'too risky for me now'; the 'in general not bad' aside nudges toward fair_hold but avoid fits best.
